title.narrative: Urban and Regional Development in NE Brazil Network of “Hub Cities"

description.narrative:
This project is embodied in a broader cooperation project established between the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and a governmental Agency named SUDENE (Superintendency for the Development of the Northeast). This referred partnership named “Northeast Regional Development'' (BRA/17/019) aims at strengthening SUDENE in its primary task of coordinating and implementing regional development in the Northeast and in the North of Minas Gerais and Espírito Santo's states.
Focused on the expansion of SUDENE's institutional capacities to formulate, implement and monitor regional development processes in its area of operation, UNDP and SUDENES’s broader project has been structured through the following components:
1. SUDENE subsidized with technical inputs for the creation of planning instruments for regional development and articulation of representative social actors in the region; 2. SUDENE with specialized knowledge and improved institutional capacities to conduct sustainable regional development processes; 3. SUDENE with strategies to operationalize sustainable regional development processes; 4. Project quality ensured to guarantee the effectiveness of technical cooperation.
The contribution from UN-Habitat is related to output 2.8 of the referred broader project second component, which aims at building a cooperation model with municipalities for urban and regional development to boost the multi-centred network of intermediary cities prioritised by SUDENE. Considering its expertise, mandate related to urban development and governance, as well as proven experience in capacity-building for local governments, UN-Habitat will have a technical supporting role in the establishment and operation of the network of intermediate cities. This shall in return contribute to the urban dimension of the existing broader cooperation between SUDENE and UNDP.
Moreover, the consolidation of a network of cities is part of the territorial strategy of the Regional Development Plan for the Northeast (PRDNE), developed by SUDENE with UNDP, with the objective of expanding the reach of regional development policies and programs.
Un-Habitat's participation also falls under the UNDP-UN-Habitat Enhanced Collaborative Framework, which states that to meet the challenges of the present and future, “both our organizations have decided to enhance their collaboration to accelerate the implementation of the New Urban Agenda (NUA) adopted at Habitat III in 2016, the Paris Agreement, and the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) globally, in accordance with the UN system-wide strategy for sustainable urbanization”.
In this context, UN-Habitat's project will focus in supporting the 51 cities prioritized by SUDENE with specific knowledge and enhanced institutional capacities to have a better coordination mechanisms and governance among them and increased capacities to reinforce their urban and territorial development processes.
To achieve these, UN-Habitat's work will focus first on mobilizing the 51 prioritized intermediate municipalities to cooperate among themselves in regional development through a network of intermediate cities. The engagement of the 51 intermediate cities will be built along the initiative through a strong communication and advocacy component and exchange with other networks. Then the capacity building component will be based on needs assessments, prioritization and a series of trainings developed using UN-Habitat's normative work, methodologies and tools. Moreover, both components will be strengthened by the methodology known as ‘challenge-driven innovation’. A central aspect of this will be the identification of urban challenges by ‘need owners’ (in this case, the municipalities) that they have not been able to solve independently. Once these challenges - related to the areas addressed in the capacity building activities - are identified, an innovation competition will be run to identify concrete and innovative solutions to the challenges. This competition has the purpose to incentivize the cities to actively participate in the network and help cities innovate and find solutions that will be tested and later, in a second phase of the project, implemented.
At the end, it is expected to all municipalities plan and articulate a vision of urban territorial development aligned to UN-Habitat's normative work, the NUA and the SDGs. Furthermore, the project will aim at having the municipalities leaderships acting as advocators for integrated territorial planning, motivating its teams to continue their collaborative work through the network of intermediary cities and allocating financial resources to enable this to flourish. At the long term, this continuity of the joint work is expected to influence the revision of instruments and policies related to urban and territorial regional development.
